info.title: Stash Studio API
info.description:
APIs for querying a shop's managed product catalog and loyalty program, for configuring the loyalty program from a partner's own tools, for asking Stash to refresh a shop's localizations, and for pulling a shop's Financial Report rows. Designed for server-to-server communication between partner backends and Stash services.

## Base URLs

| Environment | Base URL |
|---|---|
| **Test** | `https://test-api.stash.gg` |
| **Production** | `https://api.stash.gg` |

All endpoint paths below are relative to the base URL. For example, to list products in the test environment:

```
GET https://test-api.stash.gg/sdk/studio/{shop_id}/products
```

## Authentication

Every request is signed with your Ingress API key (HMAC-SHA256). Send the signature in the versioned `x-stash-hmac-signature` header.

### Setup

1. Go to **Stash Studio > Project Settings > API Secrets**
2. Click **Generate Secret** to create a new key
3. Keys created through this portal are Ingress keys by default and work with this API (this is the same key used for `/sdk/` API authentication)
4. Copy the key and store it securely; you will need it to sign every request. Studio shows the key Base64-encoded: keep it as shown, and Base64-decode it to raw bytes when you sign

### Signing a Request

1. Take the current time as a Unix timestamp in **milliseconds**, for example `1790000000000`
2. Build the string to sign as `{timestamp}.{body}`. For GET requests `{body}` is empty. For PUT and POST requests it is the **request body exactly as you send it** (the same bytes; do not re-serialize the JSON after signing). Stash verifies the signature against those exact bytes for bodies up to 18 KiB (18,432 bytes); a larger body may be refused with `401` even when it is correctly signed
3. Base64-decode your Ingress API key to raw bytes, compute HMAC-SHA256 of that string keyed with those bytes, and Base64-encode the result. Signing with the encoded key text produces a signature Stash rejects
4. Send the header `x-stash-hmac-signature: v1;{shopId};{timestamp};{base64Signature}`. The timestamp must be within 5 minutes of Stash server time

### Example (bash and python)

Keep the key, exactly as Studio shows it, in a file with owner-only permissions or in a secret store, and read and Base64-decode it inside the signing process. Never pass it as a command-line argument: process listings and shell history can capture it.

```bash
# sign <body>: prints the header value for the exact body you are about to
# send. Every request gets its own timestamp and signature.
sign() {
  local ts sig
  ts=$(($(date +%s) * 1000))
  sig=$(TS="$ts" BODY="$1" python3 - <<'PY'
import base64, hashlib, hmac, os
key = base64.b64decode(open(os.path.expanduser('~/.stash/ingress-key'), 'rb').read().strip())
msg = (os.environ['TS'] + '.' + os.environ['BODY']).encode()
print(base64.b64encode(hmac.new(key, msg, hashlib.sha256).digest()).decode())
PY
)
  printf 'v1;%s;%s;%s' '{shop_id}' "$ts" "$sig"
}

# GET: the signed body is the empty string.
curl -H "x-stash-hmac-signature: $(sign '')" \
  "https://test-api.stash.gg/sdk/studio/{shop_id}/products"

# PUT: sign the exact bytes you send, then send them with --data-binary,
# which keeps them intact. -d @file strips newlines, so the server would
# see different bytes from the ones you signed and reject the signature.
BODY='{"campaign":{"id":"season-1","name":"Season 1","tiers":[]}}'
curl -X PUT -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-stash-hmac-signature: $(sign "$BODY")" \
  --data-binary "$BODY" \
  "https://test-api.stash.gg/sdk/studio/{shop_id}/loyalty/config"
```

### Legacy header (deprecated)

`stash-hmac-signature` carries an untimestamped Base64 HMAC-SHA256 of the body alone (empty string for GET). The catalog and loyalty read endpoints still accept it, but it is replayable, so use the versioned header for new integrations. The configuration write, `PUT /sdk/studio/{shop_id}/loyalty/config`, the localization refresh, `POST /sdk/studio/{shop_id}/localizations/refresh`, and the transaction records, `GET /sdk/studio/{shop_id}/transactions`, accept only the versioned header and answer `401` to the legacy one.

put.description: Creates or updates one loyalty campaign (season) together with the shop-level display settings, bonus definitions and reward products it depends on, and optionally activates the program. The campaign id is the upsert key: an existing id updates that season, a new id creates one. The request describes the whole season it names, so a tier or milestone omitted from it is removed from that season; bonuses and reward products are created or updated by id or SKU and never removed. Draft and scheduled seasons accept every change. An active season accepts names, descriptions, images, milestone rewards, tier earn rates and a new end date; thresholds, adding or removing tiers or milestones, the start date and reset rules are refused with FAILED_PRECONDITION listing the fields. Ended seasons are read-only. This method accepts only the versioned x-stash-hmac-signature header, signed over the request body exactly as sent; the legacy stash-hmac-signature header is rejected with UNAUTHENTICATED, because it carries no timestamp and a captured request could be replayed. Applying is idempotent: after a 500, resend the same request. Returns INVALID_ARGUMENT with per-field violations when validation fails, FAILED_PRECONDITION also when the shop's loyalty program is bound to more than one shop, PERMISSION_DENIED when the shop is not enabled for configuration writes, ABORTED when another update for the shop is in progress, and NOT_FOUND for an unknown shop.

A SKU that belongs to a sellable catalog product is refused here; reference such a product from a milestone's productRewards instead.

products.description: Reward products, created or updated by SKU. Every product listed is published on write, including one saved as a draft in Studio; leave a product out of the list to keep its Studio draft unpublished. id.description: Partner-chosen campaign identifier: letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen, up to 36 characters, not "." or "..". An existing id updates that season; a new id creates one. A new id is a season boundary for every player: milestone claims are keyed by campaign.

name.description: Display name of the season. Up to 1024 characters.

startAt.description: When the season starts (RFC 3339). Omit on a draft. A future value schedules the season; on activation, omit to start now. Locked once the season is active.

endAt.description: When the season ends (RFC 3339). Must be in the future when set and must not overlap another season. Omit for an open-ended season. May be changed on an active season.

currency.description: What happens to loyalty currency balances.

reset.description: What happens to a player's points, milestone claims and currency when they first arrive in this season. On create, omit to use the defaults: points carry, milestone claims reset, currency carries. On update, omit to leave the stored rules unchanged. Accepted only on shops whose loyalty points are held by Stash; GetLoyaltyConfig omits it for other shops. Locked once the season is active.

iconUrl.description: Tier icon URL, up to 1024 characters. Partner-hosted https URL; the hostname must be on the shop's image allowlist.

post.description: Asks Stash to refresh the shop's localizations from its enabled localization source, for example after the source file changes. The request body is the empty JSON object {}. This method accepts only the versioned x-stash-hmac-signature header, signed over the request body exactly as sent ({}); the legacy stash-hmac-signature header is rejected with UNAUTHENTICATED, because it carries no timestamp and a captured request could be replayed. The shop in the signature header must equal the shop_id in the path. A successful response means the refresh is durably queued, not that the import has completed or that the storefront shows the result. Repeated calls are safe, so retry after UNAVAILABLE or a timeout with a fresh timestamp and signature. Returns UNAUTHENTICATED when the signature is missing, invalid, outside the time window, sent in the legacy header, or names a different shop or one Stash does not know; FAILED_PRECONDITION when the shop has no enabled localization source; and UNAVAILABLE when the refresh could not be queued, in which case retry.

accepted.description: true once the refresh is durably queued; not import completion or storefront visibility.

schema.description: Acknowledgement that the refresh was queued.
schema.title: Refresh Localizations Response

parameters.description: Shop identifier from Stash Studio. Must equal the shop in the x-stash-hmac-signature header.

get.description: Lists the rows of the shop's Financial Report, the settled-transaction report you reconcile payouts against, for a time window. Each record is one report row, with that row's meaning, signs and settlement dating, so the totals of the records equal the report and the payout. Join records to your purchases by transaction_id; upsert them by record_id. One transaction_id can have several payment records: failed attempts before a successful one, and rarely a second successful payment. A purchase that Stash granted can have no successful payment record when the capture failed after the grant. Set start_at and end_at (RFC 3339) to the window [start_at, end_at): start_at is inclusive, end_at is exclusive, end_at must be later than start_at, and the window is at most 31 days. A record is in the window when its ts is. An end_at later than available_until is accepted: the response then covers [start_at, available_until), and you pull again later from available_until. Records are ordered by ts, then record_id. To read all records of a window, send next_page_token as page_token, with the same start_at and end_at, until next_page_token is absent. Each page reports its as_of. as_of identifies one snapshot of the shop's report data, and one snapshot covers every month, final and preliminary. Every page of one walk comes from the snapshot of its first page, because the page_token carries it. If Stash rebuilds the report during a walk, the next page request returns ABORTED. Then start the window again from the first page, without page_token, and delete no record because of that walk. An empty window returns an empty records list, not an error. A record is final when the final report for its period exists; Stash generates it on day 5 of the next month (UTC). A final record never changes. A preliminary record (final is false) can change or disappear without a notice. On every re-pull, replace all preliminary records of the pulled window with what the response returns, and upsert the others by record_id. Re-pull a window until day 5 (UTC) of the month after the window's last month has passed and the final reports exist, whatever the window returned; then pull it one last time. On each record, merchant.payout = merchant.amount - merchant.channel_fees - merchant.tax - merchant.stash_fee + merchant.stash_fee_waived. The deductions are positive when charged on the row and negative when credited back, so subtract them as they are; do not change their signs, and do not filter records by sign. Add amounts only within one merchant.currency. This method accepts only the versioned x-stash-hmac-signature header, signed over the empty body because this is a GET request; the legacy stash-hmac-signature header is rejected with UNAUTHENTICATED, because it carries no timestamp and a captured request could be replayed. The shop in the signature header must equal the shop_id in the path. Returns UNAUTHENTICATED when the signature is missing, invalid, outside the 5-minute time window, sent in the legacy header, or names a different shop or one Stash does not know; INVALID_ARGUMENT for a missing or malformed start_at or end_at, an end_at that is not later than start_at, a window longer than 31 days, a limit outside 1 to 100, a malformed page_token, or a page_token sent with a different window; ABORTED when Stash rebuilt the report after the page_token was issued, in which case start the window again from the first page without page_token, because a retry with the same page_token fails again; and UNAVAILABLE when the data cannot be read, in which case retry with a fresh timestamp and signature.

recordId.description: Identifies this report row. Unique within the shop and stable across report regenerations. Use it to upsert your copy of each row; use transaction_id to join rows to your purchases.

transactionId.description: The transaction ID of the sale: the same value Stash sends as transaction_id in ConfirmPayment. Join records to your own purchase records by it. Every row of one sale shares it: its payments, including failed attempts, its refunds, disputes and adjustments. It does not identify a row; use record_id for that.

type.description: The report's type column. Values today: "payment", "refund", "dispute", "adjustment". The set is open: store a record with a value you do not know, do not reject it. A sale's failed payment attempts are payment records with charge.status "failed" and the sale's transaction_id; they carry no money except a possible processor fee.

orderId.description: The report's order_id column: the checkout order the charge belongs to. Use transaction_id as your join key; this field is for matching the report CSV. Absent when the report row has none.

ts.description: The report's ts column: the settlement time. It is the charge time for a failed payment and for rows from before Stash's settlement-dating cutover. The window filters on it.

chargedAt.description: The report's ts__charged column: when the player was charged.

settledAt.description: The report's ts__settled column: when the row settled. Absent when the row has not settled, for example a failed payment.

period.description: The report's period__year and period__month columns as YYYY-MM: the month of ts, which is the month of the report that carries the row.

final.description: True when the final report for period exists. Stash generates it on day 5 of the next month (UTC). A final record never changes. A preliminary record (false) can change or disappear. The final report is not a claim that every sale of the month is in it: a sale that settles after day 5 lands in the following period, with that period's ts, so a closed period never gains a record.

id.description: The report's charge__id column. Every row of one charge, its payment, refunds, disputes and adjustments, shares it.

status.description: The report's charge__status column. The set is open: store a value you do not know. Today: a payment is "succeeded" or "failed"; a refund is "succeeded"; a dispute is "won", "lost", or any other value, such as "succeeded" or "needs_response", which means the dispute is open; an adjustment is "applied".

currency.description: The report's charge__currency column: the ISO 4217 currency code in uppercase that the player paid in (for example "EUR").

amount.description: The report's charge__amount column: what the player paid, tax included, in the charge currency, signed as in the report. Major units, as a decimal string; parse it as a decimal, never as floating point.

taxAmount.description: The report's charge__tax_amount column: the tax in the charge currency. Major units, as a decimal string; parse it as a decimal, never as floating point.

billingCountry.description: The report's charge__billing_country column: Stash's best-known player location as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in uppercase. It is not a verified billing address.

failureMessage.description: The report's charge__failure_message column: the payment provider's failure text. Set on failed payments. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

failureReason.description: The report's charge__failure_reason column: Stash's normalized decline reason, an open set such as "insufficient_funds" or "card_expired". Set on failed payments. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

description.description: The report's charge__description column: the purchase description. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

cart.description: The report's charge__cart column: the cart summary at checkout. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

cartId.description: The report's charge__cart_id column: the cart the charge paid for. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

paymentMethod.description: The report's charge__payment_method column: the payment method family, an open set such as "card", "paypal", "apple_pay", "google_pay". Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

paymentSource.description: The report's charge__payment_source column: how the purchase started, an open set such as "Cart" or "StashPay". Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

billingState.description: The report's charge__billing_state column: the state or region of the billing address. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

cardCountry.description: The report's charge__card__country column: the country of the card issuer, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in uppercase. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

cardBrand.description: The report's charge__card__brand column: the card brand, for example "visa". Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

cardFunding.description: The report's charge__card__funding column: the card funding type: "credit", "debit", "prepaid" or "unknown". The set is open. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

cardNetwork.description: The report's charge__card__network column: the card network. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

charge.description: The charge columns of the report row (charge__*).
charge.title: Transaction Record Charge

currency.description: The report's merchant__currency column: the payout currency, an ISO 4217 code in uppercase (for example "USD").

exchangeRate.description: The report's merchant__exchange_rate column: units of the payout currency per one unit of the charge currency that Stash applied. A decimal string; parse it as a decimal, never as floating point.

amount.description: The report's merchant__amount column: the gross settled amount. Negative on a refund and on a dispute withdrawal; zero on a failed payment. Major units, as a decimal string; parse it as a decimal, never as floating point.

channelFees.description: The report's merchant__channel_fees column: the payment processor's fee. Positive when charged on the row, negative when credited back. Usually not credited back on a refund. Zero by design under bundled pricing. Major units, as a decimal string; parse it as a decimal, never as floating point.

tax.description: The report's merchant__tax column: the tax withheld. Positive when charged on the row, negative when credited back (most refunds). Major units, as a decimal string; parse it as a decimal, never as floating point.

stashFee.description: The report's merchant__stash_fee column: the Stash fee. Positive when charged on the row, negative when credited back (most refunds). Major units, as a decimal string; parse it as a decimal, never as floating point.

stashFeeWaived.description: The report's merchant__stash_fee_waived column: the part of the Stash fee that Stash waived. Usually zero or positive; negative when a refund reverses a waiver. Major units, as a decimal string; parse it as a decimal, never as floating point.

payout.description: The report's merchant__payout column: what Stash owes the shop for this row: amount - channel_fees - tax - stash_fee + stash_fee_waived. Can be negative. Major units, as a decimal string; parse it as a decimal, never as floating point.

merchant.description: The merchant columns of the report row (merchant__*): the settled amounts and the payout.
merchant.title: Transaction Record Merchant

taxCountry.description: The report's tax_country column: the country used for the tax calculation, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in uppercase.

taxRatePercent.description: The report's tax_rate_percent column: the tax rate applied, in percent, for example "19.0000". Absent when the row has no rated tax line. A decimal string; parse it as a decimal, never as floating point.

shopName.description: The report's shop_name column: the shop's display name. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

purchaseTaxCalculationId.description: The report's purchase_tax_calculation_id column: identifies the tax calculation behind the row's tax. Quote it when you report a suspected tax error. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

creatorCodeId.description: The report's creator_code_id column: the creator code attributed to the purchase. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

creatorCode.description: The report's creator_code column: the code as the player entered it. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

creatorCodeName.description: The report's creator_code_name column: the creator's display name at purchase time. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

items.description: One row of the shop's Financial Report, with that row's meaning, signs and settlement dating.
items.title: Transaction Record

records.description: The records on this page, ordered by ts, then record_id. Empty when the window has no records.

nextPageToken.description: Send this value as page_token to read the next page. Present when more records exist in the covered window; absent on the last page.

asOf.description: When Stash built the snapshot of the shop's report data behind this page (RFC 3339, UTC). One snapshot covers every month, final and preliminary, so the pages of a window that spans months carry the same value. Every page of one walk carries the value of its first page. If Stash rebuilds the data during a walk, the next page request returns ABORTED.

availableUntil.description: The end of the report data available now (RFC 3339, UTC). The response covers [start_at, min(end_at, available_until)). It is not a completeness bound: a later report can still add records before it, because records are dated by settlement and payment providers report settlements late. The re-pull rule brings you those records. When available_until is earlier than end_at, pull again later from available_until.

schema.description: One page of a shop's Financial Report rows for a time window.
schema.title: List Transactions Response

recordId.description: Identifies this report row. Unique within the shop and stable across report regenerations. Use it to upsert your copy of each row; use transaction_id to join rows to your purchases.

transactionId.description: The transaction ID of the sale: the same value Stash sends as transaction_id in ConfirmPayment. Join records to your own purchase records by it. Every row of one sale shares it: its payments, including failed attempts, its refunds, disputes and adjustments. It does not identify a row; use record_id for that.

type.description: The report's type column. Values today: "payment", "refund", "dispute", "adjustment". The set is open: store a record with a value you do not know, do not reject it. A sale's failed payment attempts are payment records with charge.status "failed" and the sale's transaction_id; they carry no money except a possible processor fee.

orderId.description: The report's order_id column: the checkout order the charge belongs to. Use transaction_id as your join key; this field is for matching the report CSV. Absent when the report row has none.

ts.description: The report's ts column: the settlement time. It is the charge time for a failed payment and for rows from before Stash's settlement-dating cutover. The window filters on it.

chargedAt.description: The report's ts__charged column: when the player was charged.

settledAt.description: The report's ts__settled column: when the row settled. Absent when the row has not settled, for example a failed payment.

period.description: The report's period__year and period__month columns as YYYY-MM: the month of ts, which is the month of the report that carries the row.

final.description: True when the final report for period exists. Stash generates it on day 5 of the next month (UTC). A final record never changes. A preliminary record (false) can change or disappear. The final report is not a claim that every sale of the month is in it: a sale that settles after day 5 lands in the following period, with that period's ts, so a closed period never gains a record.

id.description: The report's charge__id column. Every row of one charge, its payment, refunds, disputes and adjustments, shares it.

status.description: The report's charge__status column. The set is open: store a value you do not know. Today: a payment is "succeeded" or "failed"; a refund is "succeeded"; a dispute is "won", "lost", or any other value, such as "succeeded" or "needs_response", which means the dispute is open; an adjustment is "applied".

currency.description: The report's charge__currency column: the ISO 4217 currency code in uppercase that the player paid in (for example "EUR").

amount.description: The report's charge__amount column: what the player paid, tax included, in the charge currency, signed as in the report. Major units, as a decimal string; parse it as a decimal, never as floating point.

taxAmount.description: The report's charge__tax_amount column: the tax in the charge currency. Major units, as a decimal string; parse it as a decimal, never as floating point.

billingCountry.description: The report's charge__billing_country column: Stash's best-known player location as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in uppercase. It is not a verified billing address.

failureMessage.description: The report's charge__failure_message column: the payment provider's failure text. Set on failed payments. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

failureReason.description: The report's charge__failure_reason column: Stash's normalized decline reason, an open set such as "insufficient_funds" or "card_expired". Set on failed payments. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

description.description: The report's charge__description column: the purchase description. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

cart.description: The report's charge__cart column: the cart summary at checkout. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

cartId.description: The report's charge__cart_id column: the cart the charge paid for. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

paymentMethod.description: The report's charge__payment_method column: the payment method family, an open set such as "card", "paypal", "apple_pay", "google_pay". Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

paymentSource.description: The report's charge__payment_source column: how the purchase started, an open set such as "Cart" or "StashPay". Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

billingState.description: The report's charge__billing_state column: the state or region of the billing address. Absent when the shop's report does not carry this column or the row has no value.

hmac.description: Versioned HMAC-SHA256 signature for server-to-server requests to this API (your backend calling Stash), as opposed to client-side operations. Recommended over the deprecated legacyHmac scheme for the best security. Header format: v1;{shopId};{unixMillisTimestamp};{base64Signature} (semicolon-delimited). {base64Signature} is the base64-encoded HMAC-SHA256 of the string {unixMillisTimestamp}.{requestBody} signed with your Ingress API key, where {requestBody} is the request JSON exactly as sent for POST and PUT requests and empty for GET requests. The Ingress API key Stash Studio shows is base64-encoded: base64-decode it and use the resulting raw bytes as the HMAC key; signing with the encoded text produces a signature Stash rejects. The timestamp must be within 5 minutes of Stash server time. Your shopId is your immutable shop identifier; it and your Ingress API key are available in Stash Studio under Project Settings > API Secrets.
hmac.name: x-stash-hmac-signature

legacyHmac.description: DEPRECATED: use the versioned hmac scheme (x-stash-hmac-signature) instead for the best security. HMAC-SHA256 signature generated by signing the request body (empty string for GET requests) with the Ingress API key from Stash Studio. Base64-encoded. Accepted by the catalog and loyalty read endpoints only; UpdateLoyaltyConfig, RefreshLocalizations and ListTransactions reject it with UNAUTHENTICATED because it carries no timestamp.
